methodology: Advanced design methodology rules extracted from comprehensive book research. Each rule includes its exact source and the specific page/chapter where the principle originates.

bringhurst.source: The Elements of Typographic Style, 4th Ed. (Robert Bringhurst)

verticalRhythm.rule: All vertical spacing must be a multiple of the baseline grid unit (body line-height x body font-size)
verticalRhythm.derivation: Every margin, padding, and gap should equal N x 24px (or N x 12px for half-line adjustments)
verticalRhythm.source: Ch. 2.2 'Choose a basic leading that suits the typeface, text, and measure'

opticalMarginAlignment.rule: Hanging punctuation and optical margin alignment: punctuation marks, bullets, and quote marks should hang outside the text margin for visual alignment
opticalMarginAlignment.source: Ch. 2.3 'Add and delete vertical space in measured intervals'

paragraphIndent.rule: First paragraph after heading: no indent. Subsequent paragraphs: indent 1em OR use paragraph spacing (not both)

smallCaps.rule: Acronyms and abbreviations in running text should use small caps (not full caps) at approximately 1.1em letter-spacing
smallCaps.source: Ch. 3.2 'Use titling figures with full caps and small caps with text figures'

figureTypes.rule: Body text uses oldstyle (text) figures. Tabular data uses lining (titling) figures for column alignment

widowsOrphans.rule: Never leave fewer than 2 lines of a paragraph at the bottom (orphan) or top (widow) of a column/page

measureFormula.rule: Optimal measure = font-size x 2.5 x alphabet-length-ratio. For 16px body: 40-75 characters. For multi-column: shorter measure (40-50 characters)

typographicColor.rule: Consistent 'color' (visual density) across text blocks. Avoid rivers of white space in justified text. Prefer ragged-right for narrow measures (<50ch)

hicksLaw.formula: RT = a + b x log2(n+1) where n = number of choices
hicksLaw.practicalLimit: Navigation: max 7 items. Actions per screen: max 5. Choices requiring decision: max 3 prominently displayed
hicksLaw.reducingComplexity: Group related items. Use progressive disclosure. Provide defaults for common choices.

fittsLaw.formula: MT = a + b x log2(2D/W) where D=distance to target, W=target width
fittsLaw.practicalApplication: Primary CTA: large (min 44px), close to cursor rest position. Destructive actions: smaller, farther from primary flow.
fittsLaw.cornerAndEdgeTargets: Buttons at screen edges are effectively infinite-width targets on desktop (Fitts's principle of infinite edges)

jakobsLaw.rule: Users spend most time on OTHER sites. They expect your site to work the same way. Use familiar patterns unless there's strong reason not to.
jakobsLaw.implications: Primary nav: top or left. Close button: top-right. Form submit: bottom of form. Logo: top-left links to home.

millerLaw.rule: Average person can hold 7 plus-or-minus 2 items in working memory. ORGANIZE into chunks of 5-9 items maximum.
millerLaw.chunkingStrategy: Phone numbers: 3-3-4. Credit cards: 4-4-4-4. Long lists: groups of 5. Tab bars: max 5 items.

dohertyThreshold.rule: System responses under 400ms maintain user flow state. Above 400ms: user attention wavers. Above 1000ms: user feels system is unresponsive.
dohertyThreshold.uiImplication: Loading feedback appears at 200ms. Skeleton screens at 300ms. Full spinner at 1000ms.

aestheticUsability.rule: Users perceive aesthetically pleasing designs as MORE USABLE than they actually are. Visual polish directly impacts perceived performance.
aestheticUsability.implication: Invest in visual consistency, spacing precision, and typographic quality — they measurably improve user satisfaction scores.

vonRestorff.rule: An item that visually stands out from a group is more likely to be remembered and acted upon.
vonRestorff.implication: One primary CTA per viewport. One highlighted navigation item. One feature card with emphasis.
vonRestorff.danger: If everything is emphasized, nothing is. Von Restorff requires restraint — the contrast must be singular.

teslersLaw.rule: Every system has inherent complexity that cannot be eliminated — only moved. If you hide it from the user, the developer must absorb it.
teslersLaw.implication: Progressive disclosure: show complexity only when needed. Smart defaults reduce visible complexity without removing capability.

postelLaw.rule: Be liberal in what you accept (inputs) and conservative in what you produce (outputs).
postelLaw.formImplication: Accept multiple date formats. Trim whitespace silently. Auto-format phone numbers. Don't reject input for trivial formatting differences.

peakEndRule.rule: Users judge an experience by its peak (most intense moment) and its end (final impression), not by average of all moments.
peakEndRule.implication: Invest in: (1) the peak moment (e.g., first-value delivery, 'aha' moment), and (2) the ending (e.g., success state, confirmation, graceful close).

zeigarnikEffect.rule: People remember incomplete tasks better than completed ones. A visible progress indicator creates psychological commitment to finish.
zeigarnikEffect.implication: Multi-step forms: always show progress. Onboarding: show completion percentage. Gamification: use progress bars for engagement.

serialPositionEffect.rule: Items at the beginning (primacy) and end (recency) of a sequence are remembered better than middle items.
serialPositionEffect.implication: Place critical navigation items first and last. Most important features in first and last positions of a list. CTAs at beginning or end of content blocks.

weinschenk.source: 100 Things Every Designer Needs to Know about People (Susan Weinschenk)

peripheralVision.rule: People are drawn to movement and contrast in peripheral vision. Animations outside the focus area are MORE distracting than those at center of attention.
peripheralVision.implication: Notification badges: use color change, not animation. Avoid decorative motion in sidebars while user focuses on content.

scanningNotReading.rule: Users scan in F-pattern (left-to-right cultures): top-left gets most attention, left edge of each line gets second-most, rest is scanned.
scanningNotReading.implication: Key information and CTAs: top-left quadrant. Labels: left-aligned. Navigation: left column or top.
scanningNotReading.source: #10 'People Scan Screens Based on Past Experience and Expectations'

attentionSpan.rule: Average sustained attention on a single task: 7-8 minutes before needing a break or change. Micro-task attention: 8 seconds before evaluation.
attentionSpan.implication: Content sections: max 7-8 scrolls/screens before natural break point. First impression: must communicate value in under 8 seconds.

groupingSuperior.rule: People remember grouped information 40% better than ungrouped. Spatial proximity creates perceived relationships.
groupingSuperior.implication: Use whitespace to group related form fields. Use cards to group related content. Use dividers between unrelated sections.

progressiveDisclosure.rule: Present only the minimum information needed for the current decision. Reveal additional options only when requested.
progressiveDisclosure.levels: Level 1: Primary action visible. Level 2: Secondary actions in dropdown/menu. Level 3: Advanced options in settings/modal.

trustIndicators.rule: Users decide trust within 50ms based on visual design. Professional aesthetics = trustworthy. Inconsistency = suspicious.
trustIndicators.implication: Spacing must be pixel-perfect. Colors must be from the token system. Typography must follow the scale. No raw values.

emotionalProcessing.rule: Emotional reactions to design happen BEFORE cognitive processing. Users feel before they think.
emotionalProcessing.implication: First impression matters more than feature completeness. Loading states should feel calm, not jarring. Error states should feel empathetic, not punitive.
emotionalProcessing.source: #96 'People Process Information Better If It Is in a Story'

krug.source: Don't Make Me Think, Revisited (Steve Krug)

trunkTest.rule: On any page, within 5 seconds a user should be able to answer: (1) What site is this? (2) What page am I on? (3) What are the major sections? (4) Where am I in the hierarchy? (5) How can I search?
trunkTest.implication: Every page needs: visible site ID (logo), page title, navigation with current indicator, breadcrumb or hierarchy cue.

noExplanationNeeded.rule: If something requires explanation, it is too complex. Self-evident > intuitive > requires explanation.
noExplanationNeeded.priorityOrder: Self-evident (no thought needed) then Intuitive (minimal thought) then Documented (requires reading)

scannable.rule: Design for scanning, not reading. Users do not read — they scan for keywords that match their goal.
scannable.techniques: Bold keywords. Use bullet lists. Short paragraphs (2-3 lines max). Clear headings that describe content below.
scannable.source: Ch. 2 'How We Really Use the Web'

clicksVsThinking.rule: Number of clicks matters less than thinking-per-click. 3 mindless clicks > 1 click requiring thought.
clicksVsThinking.implication: Guided flows with obvious next steps beat single-screen complexity. Wizards > mega-forms.

conventionsOverInnovation.rule: Consistency with conventions reduces cognitive load. Only innovate where it solves a real problem, not for novelty.

norman.source: The Design of Everyday Things (Don Norman)

affordances.rule: The perceived and actual properties of an object that determine how it could be used. A button should look pressable. A slider should look draggable.
affordances.digitalImplication: Buttons: raised appearance, cursor:pointer, label as verb. Links: underline + color. Inputs: recessed/bordered region. Sliders: track + thumb.

signifiers.rule: Affordances define what CAN be done. Signifiers communicate what SHOULD be done and WHERE. Signifiers are more important than affordances.
signifiers.digitalImplication: Arrow icons on carousels. Dots for pagination. Drag handles. Placeholder text in inputs. Required asterisks.

feedback.rule: Every action must have immediate, obvious feedback. Without feedback, users do not know if their action succeeded.
feedback.timingThresholds: Immediate (<100ms): visual state change (press effect). Soon (<1000ms): progress indication. Long (>1000ms): explicit loading state with ability to cancel.

constraints.rule: Limit possible actions to prevent errors. Physical, semantic, cultural, and logical constraints.
constraints.digitalImplication: Disabled states for invalid actions. Input masks for format constraints. Confirmation dialogs for destructive actions. Max-length on text fields.
constraints.source: Ch. 4 'Knowing What to Do: Constraints, Discoverability, and Feedback'

mappings.rule: The relationship between controls and their effects should be clear and natural. Spatial layout of controls should match spatial layout of output.
mappings.digitalImplication: Vertical slider = vertical scroll. Horizontal slider = horizontal property. Left arrow = go back. Right arrow = go forward. Top = more/bigger.

errorRecovery.rule: Design for errors. Make errors reversible. Support undo. Present clear recovery paths. Never punish users for mistakes.
errorRecovery.levels: Prevention (constraints, confirmation) > Detection (validation, feedback) > Recovery (undo, reset, clear guidance)

conceptualModels.rule: Users form mental models of how a system works. Design must match the user's model, not the implementation model.
conceptualModels.implication: File system: folders and documents (not inodes). Email: inbox, sent, trash (not database tables). Shopping: cart, checkout (not order pipeline).

threePxRule.rule: If a visual difference is less than 3px, make it exactly 0 (align perfectly) or make it clearly different (8px+). Nothing in between — it looks like a mistake.
threePxRule.implication: Alignment must be pixel-perfect or deliberately offset. Near-misses are worse than large intentional differences.

squintTest.rule: Blur your eyes or squint at the design. If the hierarchy disappears, it is too weak. You should still see 3 distinct levels of visual weight.

colorHierarchy.rule: Start with grayscale. Add color LAST. If the hierarchy works in grayscale, color only enhances it. If it fails without color, the structure is broken.

shadowHierarchy.rule: Shadow size communicates distance from the surface. Subtle (1-2px blur): slightly raised. Medium (4-8px): floating. Large (16-32px): far above (overlays).
shadowHierarchy.implication: Never use identical shadows on elements at different conceptual elevations.

borderVsShadow.rule: Borders define boundaries (same elevation). Shadows communicate elevation (different depth). Do not use both on the same element unless intentional.

densityControl.rule: Density = amount of content per viewport. High density: compact, less whitespace, smaller text. Low density: spacious, generous whitespace, larger text. Match density to context.
densityControl.contextMapping: Dashboard/data: high density. Landing page/marketing: low density. Settings/forms: medium density.

semanticColorMethod.rule: Define colors by use (primary, secondary, accent) not by hue (blue, green). Generate each as a palette of 8-10 shades. Darker shades for text, lighter for backgrounds.

opacityForConsistency.rule: Instead of adding many gray shades, use opacity on a single dark color to create consistent text hierarchy on any background.
opacityForConsistency.application: Primary text: 87% opacity. Secondary text: 60% opacity. Disabled: 38% opacity. Hint: 12% opacity.

dontDesignEveryState.rule: Design the ideal state first. Then design the edge cases: empty, loading, error, overflow, minimal content.
dontDesignEveryState.stateOrder: Ideal then Empty then Loading then Error then Overflow then Single item then Many items

sizeDontWeight.rule: To de-emphasize text, make it smaller or lighter (gray), not lighter weight. Light font-weight (300) looks weak and is harder to read than small regular-weight text.

overlappingElements.rule: Overlap elements to create visual interest and depth without adding decoration. Images breaking grid lines, cards overlapping hero sections.
overlappingElements.constraint: Only overlap when both elements have clear visual boundaries (shadow, solid background, clear contrast).

emptyStateDesign.rule: Empty states are not errors — they are opportunities. Show what WILL be here, how to get started, and preview the value of populating the content.

valHead.source: Designing Interface Animation (Val Head) + Animation for the Web

anticipation.rule: Brief preparation before the main action. A button scales down slightly (95%) before launching the action. A drawer appears at edge before sliding in.

followThrough.rule: Elements settle after arriving at their destination. Slight overshoot + correction creates natural feel. Spring physics achieve this automatically.
followThrough.amount: Overshoot 3-5% for subtle. 8-12% for playful. >15% for cartoon-like (rarely appropriate in UI).

choreography.rule: When multiple elements move, they must be coordinated. Same direction = parallel. Stagger = sequential reveal. Opposing directions = contrast/attention.
choreography.constraint: Max 3 simultaneous animations visible. More than 3 creates cognitive overload.

meaningfulTransitions.rule: Transitions should maintain context: show where content came from and where it went. Spatial transitions preserve mental model of information architecture.
meaningfulTransitions.pattern: Drill-down: slide left (deeper). Back: slide right (shallower). Open: expand from trigger. Close: collapse to trigger.

motionBudget.rule: Total animation time per user interaction should not exceed 500ms. Total animation time on page load should not exceed 1000ms for all elements combined.

compositionIntegrity.rule: A molecule is a MEANINGFUL combination of atoms — not just atoms sitting next to each other. The combination must create a distinct functional unit.
compositionIntegrity.test: If removing one atom does not change the component's purpose, it is not a true molecule — it is a layout.

contextIndependence.rule: Atoms and molecules must be context-independent. They work anywhere. Context is provided by organisms and templates.
contextIndependence.implication: A Button atom works in a form, a card, a toolbar, or a modal. It does not know or care about its parent.

interfaceInventory.rule: Before designing new components, inventory all existing ones. Capture: every button variant, every heading style, every card pattern, every form layout.
interfaceInventory.purpose: Identify inconsistencies, redundancies, and true system boundaries before introducing new patterns.

patternVariation.rule: Variations must be intentional, not accidental. If two buttons look different, they should BEHAVE differently. Same behavior = same appearance.

muellerBrockmann.source: Grid Systems in Graphic Design (Josef Mueller-Brockmann)

gridAsInfrastructure.rule: The grid is not a constraint — it is infrastructure that enables creative freedom within order. Every element should relate to the grid.

moduleProportion.rule: Grid modules should have aesthetically pleasing proportions. Common ratios: 1:1 (square), 2:3 (golden approximation), 3:4 (photographic), 5:8 (golden).
moduleProportion.applicationInUI: Card aspect ratios: 3:4 for portrait, 16:9 for landscape, 1:1 for avatar. Image containers: match content orientation.

marginProportion.rule: Page margins should relate proportionally to columns and gutters. Classical proportion: margin >= gutter. Top margin < bottom margin (content floats upward visually).

gridBreaking.rule: Strategic grid-breaking creates emphasis. An element that intentionally breaks the grid draws more attention than one that follows it. Use sparingly — max 1 break per viewport.

bookVerifiedCorrections.description: Corrections and enhancements based on actual extracted book text (PDF->markdown verified readings)

workingMemoryUpdate.previousRule: Miller's Law: 7±2 items in working memory
workingMemoryUpdate.correctedRule: Working memory holds 3-4 items, not 7. Miller's original 7±2 applies to SHORT-TERM memory, but working memory (active manipulation) is limited to 3-4 items.
workingMemoryUpdate.exactQuote: Recent research now shows that the 'magical' number is four. People can hold three or four things in working memory as long as they aren't distracted.
workingMemoryUpdate.source: 100 Things Every Designer Needs to Know about People, Ch.20 'People Remember Only Four Items at Once' (Susan Weinschenk)
workingMemoryUpdate.designImplication: Navigation groups: max 4 items per visual cluster (not 7). Tab bars: max 5 items (4 + home). Form field groups: max 4-5 fields before a visual break. Card grids: show 3-4 items per row for comparison.
workingMemoryUpdate.confidenceLevel: HIGH - direct book quote, supersedes traditional 7±2 for UI design contexts

chunkingStrategy.rule: You can use more pieces of information as long as you group and chunk. Grouping with visual proximity enables processing beyond the 4-item limit.
chunkingStrategy.exactQuote: If you could limit the information you give people to four items, that would actually be a great idea, but you don't have to be that drastic. You can use more pieces of information as long as you group and chunk.
chunkingStrategy.designImplication: Display more than 4 items only when they are clearly chunked into groups of 3-4 with visual separators (whitespace, dividers, headers). Unchunked lists should max at 4 visible items.

labelPlacementVerified.rule: Labels above fields are optimal for mobile. On desktop, labels can be left-aligned when form density matters, but above-field is always safe.
labelPlacementVerified.exactQuote: We could avoid this problem by always putting the labels above the fields... On mobile, labels are positioned above the fields so they're visible when you need them.
labelPlacementVerified.source: Designing UX Forms (Jessica Enders), Ch.4-51 to 4-53
labelPlacementVerified.designImplication: Mobile: ALWAYS labels above fields. Desktop: labels above by default, left-aligned only when density justifies it and testing confirms no usability regression.

atomicDesignBoundaries.atomDefinition: Atoms are the smallest functional unit that cannot be broken further without losing their meaning.
atomicDesignBoundaries.moleculeDefinition: Molecules are groups of two or more atoms held together — they function as a unit.
atomicDesignBoundaries.organismDefinition: Organisms are relatively complex UI components composed of groups of molecules and/or atoms that form distinct sections of an interface.
exactQuotes: atoms are the smallest functional unit
Organisms form distinct sections of an interface
atomicDesignBoundaries.designImplication: Test: if removing one child doesn't change the component's identity/purpose, it's not a true molecule. Organisms must own a 'distinct section' — they represent identifiable regions of the page.

dohertyThresholdVerified.rule: System response must be under 400ms to maintain productivity and user flow state.
dohertyThresholdVerified.exactQuote: Productivity soars when a computer and its users interact at a pace (<400 ms) that ensures that neither has to wait on the other.
dohertyThresholdVerified.source: Laws of UX (Jon Yablonski), Ch.10 'Doherty Threshold'
dohertyThresholdVerified.keyTakeaway: Provide system feedback within 400 ms in order to keep users' attention and increase productivity.
dohertyThresholdVerified.designImplication: Any interaction without visual feedback at 400ms needs a loading indicator. Transitions > 400ms feel sluggish. Skeleton screens should appear at 200-300ms, full loading states at 400ms.

formCompletionResearch.rule: Every additional form question reduces completion rate and data quality while increasing error rates.
formCompletionResearch.exactQuote: Every additional question on a form reduces the completion rate and data quality, while also increasing the rate of errors. So we must have justification for each and every question.
formCompletionResearch.source: Designing UX Forms (Jessica Enders), early chapter on form length
formCompletionResearch.designImplication: Every form field must be justified. Default: remove fields unless there's explicit business requirement. Progressive disclosure: only show fields when preceding answers indicate they're needed.

scanningBehavior.rule: Break text into chunks. Use bullets, short paragraphs, and pictures to facilitate scanning.
scanningBehavior.exactQuote: Break text up into chunks. Use bullets, short paragraphs, and pictures.
scanningBehavior.designImplication: Body text: max 2-3 sentences per paragraph. Lists: use bullet points for 3+ related items. Content blocks: separate with visual breaks every 4-5 items.

astryxTieredLineHeight.rule: Line-height varies by font size tier, not as a single fixed value. Larger text needs tighter leading; smaller text needs looser.

smallText.rationale: Small text needs generous leading for readability

mediumText.rationale: Medium headings transitional — still readable, slightly tighter

largeText.rationale: Large display text has enough internal whitespace; tight leading looks intentional

astryxTieredLineHeight.gridSnap: Computed line-height is snapped to nearest 4px increment (minimum: fontSize + 4px)
astryxTieredLineHeight.source: astryx-main/packages/core/src/theme/expandTypeScale.ts (Meta production code, verified via code audit)
astryxTieredLineHeight.designImplication: Replace the single lineHeightBody value with a tiered function. ProdigeUI tokens should compute line-height from font-size, not store a single ratio.

astryxRadiusSemantics.rule: Border radius should use semantic naming based on element role, not arbitrary size labels.

scale.inner: base×1 (4px) — internal corners within a component (chips, tags, nested elements)
scale.page: base×7 (28px) — page-level containers (modals, drawers, full-width banners)

astryxRadiusSemantics.multiplierSystem: All scalable values use: base × step × multiplier. Multiplier=0 produces brutalist. Multiplier=1.5 produces extra-rounded.
astryxRadiusSemantics.designImplication: Migrate ProdigeUI from radius.sm/md/lg/xl to radius.inner/element/container/page. Semantic names communicate the USE not the SIZE, enabling themes to scale radii proportionally.

astryxMotionRatio.rule: Animation durations use a ratio system that generates min/base/max from a single value, ensuring proportional relationships.
astryxMotionRatio.formula: min = base × ratio, max = base / ratio
astryxMotionRatio.designImplication: Replace fixed duration tokens with ratio-computed min/base/max. Map motion presets to Three Dials system: MOTION_INTENSITY low → snappy, medium → default, high → cinematic.

astryxHCTColorModel.rule: Color palette generation uses HCT (Hue-Chroma-Tone) perceptual color space instead of HSL. HCT guarantees perceptually uniform lightness across hues.
astryxHCTColorModel.advantage: In HSL, 'same lightness' produces visually different brightness (yellow appears brighter than blue at same L). HCT's Tone dimension ensures equal perceptual brightness regardless of hue.

paletteGeneration.gamutMapping: Binary search reducing chroma until color is within sRGB gamut

astryxHCTColorModel.designImplication: ProdigeUI color-palette-generation skill should recommend HCT-based generation. All tone values in the palette are perceptually equivalent in lightness — critical for consistent UI.
